newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese pound continues rise against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese pound continues rise against dollar.

text.p: The Lebanese pound continued to rise against the U.S. dollar in the week ended Friday in quiet trade, despite falling interest rates on the currency, dealers said.

The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band to 1,545.5-1,555 pounds per dollar from 1,546-1,555.50, with the dollar continuing to trade at the bottom of the band throughout the week, dealers said.

"People are still interested in investing in the Lebanese pound despite the decrease in interest rates," Nabil Abou Jaoude, treasurer and chief dealer for Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce, told Reuters.

Trade on the foreign exchange market was restricted to a very tight range of 20-25 piastres at the bid end of the central bank's intervention band, Abou Jaoude said. All dollar offers were taken up by commercial banks, he added.

Yields on Lebanese pound-denominated treasury bills also continued to fall during the week. They now stand at 14.17 percent for three-month bills, 15.89 percent for six months, 16.38 percent for 12 months and 18.12 percent for 24-month bills.
The Lebanese Banks Association also reduced the pound prime lending rate last week to 18 percent from 24 percent to catch up with the downward trend in t-bill yields.
